mn148:1.2: On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park.
mn148:1.3: There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus thus:
mn148:1.5: ‘Venerable sir,’ those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One.
mn148:2.1: ‘Bhikkhus, I shall teach you the Dhamma that is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with the right meaning and phrasing, and I shall proclaim the holy life that is utterly perfect and pure, that is to say,
mn148:2.3: Listen and heed well what I shall say.’
mn148:2.4: ‘Yes, venerable sir,’ those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One.
mn148:3.1: ‘The six bases in oneself should be understood. The six external bases should be understood. The six bodies of consciousness should be understood. The six bodies of contact should be understood. The six bodies of feeling should be understood. The six bodies of craving should be understood.
mn148:4.1: “The six bases in oneself should be understood”—
mn148:4.2: so it was said. And with reference to what was this said?
mn148:4.3: The eye base, the ear base, the nose base, the tongue base, the body base, the mind base.
mn148:4.4: “The six bases in oneself should be understood”—
mn148:4.5: so it was said, and it was with reference to this that it was said.
mn148:5.1: “The six external bases should be understood”—
mn148:5.2: so it was said. And with reference to what was this said?
mn148:5.3: The form base, the sound base, the odour base, the flavour base, the tangible base, the dhamma base.
mn148:5.4: “The six external bases should be understood”—
mn148:5.5: so it was said, and it was with reference to this that it was said.
mn148:6.1: “The six bodies of consciousness should be understood”—
mn148:6.2: so it was said. And with reference to what was this said?

mn148:6.4: dependent on the ear and sounds, ear-consciousness arises;

mn148:6.6: dependent on the tongue and flavours, tongue-consciousness arises;

mn148:6.8: dependent on the mind and dhammas, mind-consciousness arises.
mn148:6.9: “The six bodies of consciousness should be understood”—
mn148:6.10: so it was said, and it was with reference to this that it was said.
mn148:7.1: “The six bodies of contact should be understood”—
mn148:7.2: so it was said. And with reference to what was this said?
mn148:7.3: Dependent on the eye and forms, eye-consciousness arises; the meeting of the three is contact;
mn148:7.4: dependent on the ear and sounds, ear-consciousness arises; the meeting of the three is contact;

mn148:7.10: so it was said, and it was with reference to this that it was said.

mn148:8.8: dependent on the mind and dhammas, mind-consciousness arises; the meeting of the three is contact; with contact as condition there is feeling.

mn148:8.10: so it was said, and it was with reference to this that it was said.
mn148:9.1: “The six bodies of craving should be understood”—
mn148:9.2: so it was said. And with reference to what was this said?
mn148:9.3: Dependent on the eye and forms, eye-consciousness arises; the meeting of the three is contact; with contact as condition, feeling; with feeling as condition, craving;

mn148:28.1: Bhikkhus, dependent on the eye and forms, eye-consciousness arises; the meeting of the three is contact; with contact as condition there arises what is felt as pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant.
mn148:28.2: If, when touched by pleasant feeling, one relishes it, affirms it, and remains holding to it,
mn148:28.3: then the underlying tendency to lust underlies that.
mn148:28.4: If, when touched by painful feeling, one sorrows, grieves and laments, beating one’s breast one weeps and becomes distraught,
mn148:28.5: then the underlying tendency to resistance underlies that.
mn148:28.6: If, when touched by neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, one does not understand as it actually is the origin, the disappearance, the gratification, the danger, and the escape in the case of that feeling,
mn148:28.7: then the underlying tendency to ignorance underlies that.
mn148:28.8: That one shall make an end of suffering without abandoning the underlying tendency to lust for pleasant feeling, without eliminating the underlying tendency to resistance to painful feeling, without abolishing the underlying tendency to ignorance of neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, without abandoning ignorance, and without arousing true knowledge, here and now—this is not possible.

mn148:34.1: Bhikkhus, dependent on the eye and forms, eye-consciousness arises; the meeting of the three is contact; with contact as condition there arises what is felt as pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant.
mn148:34.2: If, when touched by pleasant feeling, one does not relish it, does not affirm it, and does not remain holding to it,
mn148:34.3: then no underlying tendency to lust underlies that.
mn148:34.4: If, when touched by painful feeling, one does not sorrow, does not grieve and lament, does not, beating one’s breast, weep and become distraught,
mn148:34.5: then no underlying tendency to resistance underlies that.
mn148:34.6: If, when touched by neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, one understands as it actually is the origin, the disappearance, the gratification, the danger, and the escape in the case of that feeling,
mn148:34.7: then no underlying tendency to ignorance underlies that.
mn148:34.8: That one shall make an end of suffering by abandoning the underlying tendency to lust for pleasant feeling, by eliminating the underlying tendency to resistance to painful feeling, by abolishing the underlying tendency to ignorance of neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, by abandoning ignorance and arousing true knowledge, here and now—this is possible.

mn148:40.1: Seeing thus, bhikkhus, the well-taught noble disciple becomes dispassionate towards the eye, becomes dispassionate towards forms, becomes dispassionate towards eye-consciousness, becomes dispassionate towards eye-contact, becomes dispassionate towards feeling, becomes dispassionate towards craving.
mn148:41.1: He becomes dispassionate towards the ear, becomes dispassionate towards sounds …
mn148:41.2: he becomes dispassionate towards the nose, becomes dispassionate towards odours …
mn148:41.3: he becomes dispassionate towards the tongue, becomes dispassionate towards flavours …
mn148:41.4: he becomes dispassionate towards the body, becomes dispassionate towards tangibles …
mn148:41.5: he becomes dispassionate towards the mind, becomes dispassionate towards dhammas, becomes dispassionate towards mind-consciousness, becomes dispassionate towards mind-contact, becomes dispassionate towards feeling, becomes dispassionate towards craving.
mn148:41.6: Being dispassionate, his greed fades away; with the fading of greed his mind is liberated. When it is liberated there comes the knowledge: ‘It is liberated.’
mn148:41.7: He understands: ‘Birth is exhausted, the life divine has been lived, what was to be done is done, there is no more of this to come.’”
mn148:41.8: This is what the Blessed One said.
mn148:41.9: The bhikkhus were satisfied and delighted in the Blessed One’s words.
mn148:41.10: And while this discourse was being spoken, the minds of as many as sixty bhikkhus were liberated from the taints by not clinging.
mn148:41.11: The Discourse on the Six Sixes, the sixth, is finished.
